subject.title: [security] Lambda cleanup trusts tag-only instances without a local claim

question: Should Lambda direct-provider cleanup and release fail closed without an unchanged local claim before terminating instances or deleting Lambda SSH keys?
rationale: The source-level issue is clear, but the permanent security boundary must decide which Lambda recovery or reclaim exceptions remain valid for failed creates and intentionally lost local state.

options.title: Require exact local claims
options.body: Treat provider tags as discovery hints, skip or report unclaimed Lambda inventory, and allow only explicit recovery/reclaim claims to authorize destructive cleanup.

options.title: Disable destructive Lambda cleanup temporarily
options.body: Pause Lambda cleanup deletes until the provider can prove claim-bound ownership for every destructive path.

options.title: Keep tag-only cleanup
options.body: Preserve current orphan-reclaim behavior but accept that provider labels remain destructive authority for Lambda resources.

recommendation.title: Require exact local claims
recommendation.body: Treat provider tags as discovery hints, skip or report unclaimed Lambda inventory, and allow only explicit recovery/reclaim claims to authorize destructive cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: Current release/current-main owner is best positioned to decide the security-boundary tradeoff for the just-shipped provider while routing implementation back to the Lambda contributors.
